lines: A button with a trigger, a gate and a toggle output, and a stepped constant voltage source
Pressing it fires the trigger output, holds the gate output high, flips the toggle output and moves the constant voltage on one step
A voltage rising past 2V here does what pressing the button does
A 1ms 10V trigger each time the button is pressed
10V for as long as the button is held down, 0V the rest of the time
Flips between 0V and 10V on each button press
A steady voltage that steps through 1V, 5V and 10V, moving on one step each time the button is pressed
Note — this is the one module in the plugin with no polyphony; every output carries a single channel
Five offsets, each adding a fixed voltage or a whole number of semitones to a signal, or standing on its own as a voltage source
Sets the offset added on that row: -10V to 10V with the switch on VOLTS, or a whole number of semitones out to three octaves either way with it on SEMI
The signal that row's offset is added to; leave it unpatched and the row takes its signal from the nearest patched input above it
That row's signal with that row's offset added; with nothing patched into that row or any row above it, the offset alone
Switches every offset between volts, reaching -10V to 10V, and whole semitones, reaching three octaves either way
Note — the lamp beside an output is coloured to match the input whose signal that row is carrying
Multiplies and divides two voltages, with switches to scale the inputs and the result
Divides the A input by 1, 5 or 10 before the arithmetic, which brings a -5V to 5V signal down to a range of -1 to 1
Divides the B input by 1, 5 or 10 before the arithmetic, which brings a -5V to 5V signal down to a range of -1 to 1
Multiplies both results by 1, 5 or 10 on the way out
Clamps both outputs between -10V and 10V while it is on
One of the two voltages; with nothing patched here A counts as 1
The other voltage; with nothing patched here both outputs carry A on its own
A multiplied by B, after the input scaling and the output scaling
A divided by B, after the input scaling and the output scaling; while B is at 0V this holds the last result it could work out
Turns a trigger into a gate of a set length, and fires a trigger when that gate ends
Sets the length of the gate: 1ms to 10 seconds over a logarithmic sweep with the switch on LOG, or 0 to 10 seconds evenly spread with it on LIN
Switches the duration knob and the CV scaling between logarithmic and linear
Sets how far the CV input moves the gate length and in which direction; at the centre the CV input has no effect, and at either end 10V moves the length by its full range
Voltage that lengthens or shortens the gate, scaled by the CV AMT knob
A voltage rising past 2V here starts a gate; the channels patched here set the module's polyphony
10V for as long as the gate lasts
A 1ms 10V trigger the moment the gate ends
Note — the display reads out the gate length in milliseconds or seconds, and switches to the CV amount while that knob is being turned
Menu — Allow retrigger while gate is on — on by default, restarts the gate from the beginning when a trigger arrives during one; switched off, triggers arriving during a gate are ignored
Menu — Update display in real time — shows the length including the CV; switched off, the display reads the knob's own setting
Note — There is no button on the panel: the module does nothing until a voltage rises past 2V at the trigger input
Sends eight signals without cables to any Teleport Out module in the patch, under a label you type
One of eight signals carried to every Teleport Out module set to this module's label
Note — click the text box and type the label, up to four characters; it is case sensitive, and two Teleport In modules cannot share one
Receives eight signals without cables from a Teleport In module picked by label
Carries whatever is patched into the matching input of the chosen Teleport In module
Note — Click the text box to open a menu headed Select source, listing (none) and the label of every Teleport In module in the patch; this menu is on the text box, not the panel
Note — the lamp beside an output is green while the matching input at the Teleport In end has a cable in it and red while it does not
Note — With no Teleport In module anywhere in the patch, or with the source set to (none), all eight outputs rest at 0V and every lamp is dark
